topic: What happens when we send a WhatsApp message?

claims.claim: Personal WhatsApp messages are end-to-end encrypted automatically, with no setting to turn on.
Messages are secured with a lock; only the sender and the recipient have the special key.
Messages are encrypted (Signal protocol) before they leave the sender's device.
No one outside the chat, not even WhatsApp, can read personal messages.
claims.note: business chats using optional Meta services are an exception; the video covers personal chats only

claims.claim: One grey tick: the message was sent.
Two grey ticks: the message was delivered to the recipient's phone or a linked device.
Two blue ticks: the recipient has read the message.
claims.note: ticks staying grey do not prove a message is unread (read receipts may be off); not narrated as a rule

claims.claim: An undelivered message is kept on WhatsApp's servers in encrypted form for up to 30 days, then deleted.
Once delivered, messages are deleted from WhatsApp's servers.
claims.note: forwarded media may be stored temporarily in encrypted form; the video shows a text message

visual_guardrails: show a text message in a personal chat (not a business chat, not media)
the server is drawn as one illustrative building, not WhatsApp's real infrastructure
no WhatsApp logo, brand colours used generically (green chat, grey/blue ticks are UI conventions)
